title: Extreme cold
tldr: Get into a warm, dry place, replace wet clothing and add dry layers. Confusion, extreme drowsiness or loss of coordination can indicate hypothermia; call emergency services. Use safe heat and never bring grills or generators indoors.
steps: Limit outdoor exposure and protect hands, feet, head and face.
Use dry layers and blankets; warm the body gently.
Use approved heaters as directed, keep them away from combustibles and maintain CO alarms.
If heat fails, contact local warming shelters and help people with limited mobility relocate safely.
next: Keep medicines, transport and backup plans ready. Watch for numb, pale or waxy skin that may signal frostbite.
watch: Do not rub frostbitten skin or apply direct intense heat.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Use one dry room, layered clothing, blankets and insulation beneath you. Keep fuel-burning outdoor equipment outside. If you cannot keep people warm, identify a reachable warm place before they become confused or weak; do not wait for a warming centre to open.
household: Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
